thread:
ashley_support: FYI - AcmePay reported 500s and weird tokenization after we failed over to us-west-2 backup this morning. Opening thread with logs and repro.

ashley_support: customer says their invoice parser suddenly returns gibberish and token counts jumped ~3x. They included a curl call that hit our EU region but got routed to US backup.

jamal_eng: can you paste the original request (sanitized) + the response they got? also which model they were requesting?

ashley_support: pasted below (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"model":"invoice-parse-v2","input":"Invoice: ..."}'
```
They said response looked like tokenized byte artifacts (weird tokens like "Ġpaym﻿ent"). Their client logged HTTP 502 then a retry got a 200 with corrupted text.

olivia_sre: ops-bot routed to us-west-2 due to eu capacity pressure at 1719504200-1719504300 window. ops-bot, paste routing snippet?

ops-bot: routing decision: fallback_policy=region_then_capacity; selected backup region=us-west-2; selected model_variant=invoice-parse-v2-lite (compatible_by_api but not by tokenizer/vocab).

jamal_eng: ah ok — variant is a lighter quantized family that uses a different tokenizer/vocab mapping. That's our mismatch. When we fallback we should prefer tokenizer-compatible variants or perform tokenizer translation.

ashley_support: customer also flagged billing: token billing showed sudden spike for the failed requests (they saw three increments for 1 call). billing-bot, do we have meters for that session?

billing-bot: meter snapshot for acct AcmePay: 1719504215 -> +0.8 units (attempt failed), 1719504221 -> +2.6 units (retry served by lite variant), 1719504230 -> +0.0 units (client retry aborted). Total billed: 3.4 units. Correlation id: rwd-req-3f9b.

jamal_eng: the lite variant has different tokenization rules; the client considered the output invalid and retried, so they paid extra. That’s bad.

olivia_sre: short-term mitigation: we can rollback routing to strict_region_preference for AcmePay (route -> fail 5xx rather than serve incompatible variant), and credit the extra meter. I'll open a patch to routing policy for that account.

ashley_support: customer asked for repro steps — provided a minimal script to reproduce. I ran it with explicit region header + model param and got the same artifacts when allowed to fallback. Repro steps below:
```
# repro (sanitized)
for i in 1 2 3; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" \
    -d '{"model":"invoice-parse-v2","input":"Total $123.45"}' \
    https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate | jq -r .output
done
# allow eu to be marked full to force fallback
```
Response when routed to us-west-2-lite: "ĠTotalĠ$1��23.45" (corrupted spacing markers).

jamal_eng: action items from infra/eng side: 1) add variant compatibility metadata (tokenizer_id) to model catalog so router only selects tokenizer-compatible fallbacks by default; 2) make billing credit automation for failed->retry sequences where variant mismatch is detected; 3) add an alert when fallback->variant.tokenizer != requested_model.tokenizer. I'll make PRs for (1) and (3).

olivia_sre: ops: for immediate relief I'll add a route override for AcmePay and a global soft-config: prefer_tokenizer_compat=true for region fallbacks. Also increase EU burst cap for next 2 hours.

ashley_support: I'll patch the support ticket with repro, explain root cause (fallback chose quantized-lite variant with different tokenizer), and offer a credit for the overcharged tokens. Customer asked for ETA.

jamal_eng: estimate: small router change + catalog metadata - ~1 biz day for PR + canary. Billing credit automation needs product sign-off (~2-3 days).

olivia_sre: tagging @jamal_eng and @ashley_support for postmortem. Please add short timeline and proposed mitigations to the ticket. :thumbsup:

ashley_support: will do. adding links to logs and the ops decision. closing loop with customer now.
